title: More Words Than Reality
lines: More Words Than Reality examines research that looks mature before independent checks justify it.
The problem extends beyond fabricated facts to convincing architectures, tests, and validation packages.
The book separates perceived achievement from what survives comparison, execution, and attempted falsification.
It proposes tools for checking knowledge claims while preserving explicit human responsibility for value judgments.
Readers gain a framework for challenging apparent progress without dismissing useful AI-assisted research.

title: The convincing research package
lines: A theory can arrive with diagrams, code, tests, and a persuasive review of itself.
Those artifacts may still address a nearby problem rather than the intended one.
A new vocabulary can also conceal resemblance to earlier work.
The book calls attention to what remains after relevant independent checks.
Its concern is the gap between apparent maturity and a contribution that withstands scrutiny.

title: Checks need independence
lines: A proposed research system would record whether a statement is assumed, tested, or demonstrated.
Source checks, execution, baselines, and counterexamples would challenge different aspects of the claim.
The book also separates evidential assessment from decisions about what is worth pursuing.
These guardian architectures are research proposals, not established machines for certifying discovery.
Their own evaluation must resist the circular validation they are designed to expose.

title: Read against the appearance
lines: Begin with the taxonomy of illusions and its concrete tests of apparent progress.
Keep published evidence, the author's synthesis, and new proposals distinct as you read.
The institutional chapters explain why tools alone cannot repair incentives that reward appearance.
More Words Than Reality turns frustration with plausible research into an inspectable research programme.
Read it to ask what would survive if the convincing presentation were removed.
